title: Specialized Text Analysis
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of specialized text analysis and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply word counts and tokenization in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Specialized Text Analysis is part of Strings, Regular Expressions, and Text Processing. Start with word counts and tokenization and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: Text processing should distinguish matching values from near-misses and account for missing text and encoding.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Text processing should distinguish matching values from near-misses and account for missing text and encoding. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

items.title: Word Counts and Tokenization
items.text: Explain word counts and tokenization in the context of specialized text analysis, connect it to the example, and verify one expected result or edge case.

items.text: Build the smallest example for working with text corpora, inspect the returned object, and confirm its names, type and shape before using it downstream.

items.title: Introductory Sentiment and Topic Analysis
items.text: For introductory sentiment and topic analysis, parse values to a date-time class first and verify formats, timezone assumptions and a boundary date.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Test at least one matching string, one non-match and one boundary or non-ASCII value. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf does not provide an R runtime. This block is an inspectable reference example; execute it in a local R console or a reviewed R-aware environment. Static validation checks file structure, not R semantics.
content_blocks.reset_steps: No example is executed by this CodeLeaf lesson. For a local run, use synthetic data in a temporary working directory, avoid production credentials or destructive writes, and restart a clean R session to clear lesson objects.
content_blocks.limitations: Check matching and non-matching text, whitespace, missing strings and encoding assumptions. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For specialized text analysis, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
